    "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Democratic Representative Gwen Moore of Wisconsin says higher gasoline prices are deepening Americans' cost-of-living squeeze, pushing back on President Donald Trump's comments that Americans should accept paying "a tiny bit more" at the pump because of the war with Iran. Republican Representative Mike Flood of Nebraska says affordability is a concern he continues to hear from constituents, despite President Donald Trump dismissing the issue as a "hoax." Democratic Representative Greg Casar of Texas says AI CEOs should testify before Congress about employment and national security concerns surrounding the technology. (Source: Bloomberg)
    Rep. Casar on Texas Data Center Freeze
    Democratic Representative Greg Casar of Texas says AI CEOs should testify before Congress about employment and national security concerns surrounding the technology. Rep. Casar argues data center projects should be blocked if they raise electricity bills or otherwise harm the communities where they’re built. He discusses legislation that would impose a tax on large AI companies and increase the rate as unemployment rises, with revenue used to support a federal jobs program. Rep. Casar also says Democrats should focus on working people and argues Republican efforts to label Democrats communists are a familiar political tactic that won’t work. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Rep. Flood: Affordability at Center of Reelection Campaign
    Republican Representative Mike Flood of Nebraska says affordability is a concern he continues to hear from constituents, despite President Donald Trump dismissing the issue as a "hoax." Flood, who chairs the Republican Main Street Caucus, says recently passed housing legislation will help boost supply and lower home prices, though he acknowledges relief may not arrive quickly. Flood also says the US needs to "finish the job" in Iran while putting the mental health, safety and morale of American service members at the highest level of concern. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Higher Gas Costs Are ‘Busting’ Budgets: Moore
    Democratic Representative Gwen Moore of Wisconsin says higher gasoline prices are deepening Americans' cost-of-living squeeze, pushing back on President Donald Trump's comments that Americans should accept paying "a tiny bit more" at the pump because of the war with Iran. She also says Francesca Hong's strong showing in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary demonstrated the resonance of her affordability message, while arguing Democrats shouldn't be bullied by Republican efforts to characterize safety-net policies as communism.     Donald Trump can’t beat Iran and Nigel Farage can only beat a bin. When it counts, these populists are just losers | Jonathan Freedland
    The pattern in the US and Britain is clear. They serve up stunt after stunt to mask incompetence and the betrayal of all those who trusted them It’s a shame Nigel Farage ducked the announcement of his victory in the Clacton byelection, which confirmed his return as MP for the seat he had needlessly resigned from just a few weeks earlier. You’d have thought he would have loved it. It was the culmination of a stunt, an exercise in politics as performance. It was a display animated by – and seeking to inflame – grievance, a million miles away from the hard, grinding work of tackling the problems that underlie those grievances. It was an attempt to deflect scrutiny, distract attention and evade responsibility. It was, in other words, everything nationalist populists like him excel at. Indeed, the only thing. Reform UK said Farage stayed away because Essex police had warned of a “credible threat” to his security, a claim swiftly denied by Essex police. (Add a flexible approach to the truth to that list of nationalist populists’ talents.) Still, it was a slightly odd claim to make. Recall Farage’s favoured explanation – there are others – for the undeclared £5m gift he received from the Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, which prompted the very parliamentary investigation that so riled the Reform leader he felt compelled to quit his seat and seek a preemptive not guilty verdict from the people of Clacton: namely, that he needed the money to pay for private, enhanced security. It seems £5m was not quite enough to ensure the lucky recipient would be safe standing next to a man dressed as a bin.
